method: Every candidate opened and viewed. Category membership is NOT treated as evidence of subject. An image with no decision here is NOT curated and is never admitted by default.
decidedBy: build-lead visual review (single reviewer; NOT two independent reviews)

tiera-outerwear-0e07b2e685.reason: Extreme close-up of printed textile pattern. No garment silhouette, no identifiable item — subject is the fabric, not a wearable.

tiera-pants-24e666e3bd.note: Close-packed denim jeans/shorts, cropped. Strong denim material case and a genuine partial-framing case.

tiera-pants-97037f4477.note: Dark indigo jeans, front, flat on wood floor. Button fly visible. Front view of a true two-view same-item set.

tiera-pants-b0514ee815.note: Same jeans, back. Arcuate pocket stitching and a small red tab are visible. Trade-dress indicators are NOT legible brand text, so brand stays not_visible — this is a good test of whether the model over-claims a brand from trade dress alone.

tiera-bag-1d00530785.note: Open tool bag on white. A genuine bag, but a utility tool bag rather than a fashion bag — a legitimate category edge case. A small maker logo is on the product.

tiera-accessory-7a2df42046.note: Round sunglasses with THOM BROWNE NEW YORK legible on the cleaning cloth, box and case. FIRST directly brand-evidenced case in the corpus. tiera-accessory-7a2df42046.brandEvidenceSource: THOM BROWNE NEW YORK legible on the cleaning cloth, box and case in the photograph itself

tiera-top-c9ade2205d.note: Boutique interior from above, garments on racks and hangers. Genuine store_display. Wall posters depict people, but those are photographs-of-photographs rather than identifiable people present in the scene.

tiera-top-97c77cbd99.note: Sari/lehenga shop with mannequins and hanging garments. Valuable non-Western garment coverage the rest of the corpus lacks. Mannequins are not people; one distant indistinct figure sits at the left frame edge with no identifiable face.

tiera-accessory-521e3b1022.note: Three felt fedoras on purple cloth. Clean hat case, and a useful multiple-similar-items test.

tiera-bag-1610b00ea6.note: Zippered cosmetic pouch with lace trim, printed with a photographic gourd/pumpkin pattern. Adversarial in a useful way: the print depicts real objects, which could pull an identifier toward the printed content instead of the bag.

tiera-accessory-396b72f77b.note: Oversized black sunglasses resting on a concrete ledge outdoors. Clean eyewear case.

tiera-accessory-e2f0db2378.note: 1976 novelty campaign sunglasses with a chain and portrait medallions. Adversarial in a useful way: printed human faces appear ON the accessory, which should not trigger person handling.

tiera-accessory-a53e61e148.note: Flower-petal pendant on a cord, close-up. Genuine jewellery subject; petals are cropped, so it doubles as a partial-framing case.

tiera-bag-cdf287c82d.note: Small handmade button-flap pouch on a wooden surface. Genuinely soft-focus — kept deliberately as a BLUR case, with labelConfidence low to match. Material left unknown rather than guessed from a blurred image.

tiera-top-4dbef79f7b.note: Multicoloured marled knit turtleneck on a wooden artist's mannequin, with a toy bear in frame. Strong knit-material case; the extra object is tagged rather than ignored.

tiera-dress-d3a98e8fd9.note: Origami/pleated dress on a mannequin in a lit shop window at night, photographed through glass. Unusually valuable: it satisfies store_display, low_light AND the reflection/mirror stratum at once — the mirror-reversed VICTORIA'S SECRET signage is proof it is a reflection. That third-party mark is incidental, and the reflected background figures are indistinct silhouettes with no identifiable faces. Material left unknown: it reads as folded paper or coated fabric and guessing would be fabrication.

tiera-non_fashion-635218364b.note: Ceramic commemorative mug in a museum case, reading PRESTON GUILD 1842. A strong negative: legible text on a non-fashion object is exactly what could bait a spurious brand claim.

tiera-non_fashion-7f42f440f8.reason: DEFERRED for consistency with the other two bicycle images: a vehicle is present in frame. Not a quality rejection. WANTED for a later round: the frame carries a legible endorphine 5.3 wordmark, making it a strong probe for brand invention on a NON-apparel object.

tiera-non_fashion-87857eed80.note: Ceramic commemorative mug in a museum vitrine, 1862 Preston Guild Festival. Admitted as a non-fashion negative. Doubles as a false-positive probe: the object carries large legible text and a floral print, which is exactly the cue set that can push a fashion model into inventing a garment or a brand.

tiera-non_fashion-323cd4e23c.note: Second 1842 Preston Guild mug. Non-fashion negative; same false-positive probe rationale.

tiera-non_fashion-4229e3a4dc.reason: DEFERRED, not rejected on quality. A vehicle registration plate is present in frame. I will not assert it is illegible without verifying, and masking work is out of scope by owner instruction, so the case is held rather than admitted or altered.

curationRule: Owner decision 2026-07-29: face presence is NOT a blocker, and face blurring is being loosened during testing. Earlier face-only rejections are reinstated as keeps. Faces PRINTED ON garments were never a concern. Cases still record visiblePerson and faceReviewState so the corpus stays auditable if the policy tightens again.

set-fishskin-jacket.description: Hezhe (Nanai) fishskin jacket, 1875-1900, museum documentation. Four independently captured views of ONE physical garment, all CC0.
set-fishskin-jacket.note: Independently captured views carrying different evidence, not crops of one file. The material-detail view is a legitimate set member per the capture spec view taxonomy, but is NOT usable as a standalone identification case.
set-fishskin-jacket.identityEvidence: Commons filenames 01/02/03 of one museum object; confirmed visually as the same garment

set-501xx-jeans.description: One pair of dark indigo jeans, front and back, flat on a wood floor. Same garment, two independently captured views, CC BY-SA 4.0.
set-501xx-jeans.note: The back view shows arcuate pocket stitching and a small red tab. The filename says 501xx but a FILENAME is not image evidence, and no wordmark is legible, so brand stays not_visible.
set-501xx-jeans.identityEvidence: Filenames 501xx-front / 501xx-back; confirmed visually as one pair on the same floor
